title: Pathogenic B-T Cell Axis Driven by BAFF Induces Endothelial Apoptosis in SLE-PAH
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a fatal complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), yet the mechanisms linking autoimmune dysregulation to progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling are poorly defined, leading to inadequate therapies. This study investigated BAFF (B-cell activating factor), a key cytokine in SLE, as a potential driver of SLE-PAH pathogenesis. METHODS: BAFF expression was assessed in patients with SLE-PAH and animal models. Humanized BAFF-transgenic mice were generated to investigate the effects of BAFF elevation on serological, hemodynamic, and histological parameters of SLE and PAH. Single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, histological analyses, and cell-based experiments were performed to elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms. The therapeutic efficacy of the BAFF-neutralizing antibody Belimumab was tested in 2 distinct SLE-PAH animal models. RESULTS: BAFF was significantly upregulated in both SLE-PAH patient cohorts and animal models. Humanized BAFF-transgenic mice exhibited systemic B-cell hyperactivation and pulmonary infiltration and spontaneously developed hallmark features of both SLE and PAH. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of lung tissues revealed that BAFF overexpression drove the increase of a novel, disease-specific S 100a6 + mature B-cell subset, which orchestrated a pathogenic immune cascade by activating a cytotoxic Gzmk + CD8 + T-cell population via MHC-I (major histocompatibility complex class I)-mediated antigen presentation and CD80-CD28 costimulation. This B-T cell crosstalk triggered apoptosis of a susceptible endothelial cell subpopulation through Fas/Fas ligand signaling, ultimately culminating in pulmonary vascular remodeling. The BAFF-neutralizing antibody Belimumab effectively ameliorated both autoimmune and cardiopulmonary manifestations in 2 distinct SLE-PAH animal models, while improving survival. CONCLUSIONS: These findings establish BAFF as a key mediator in SLE-PAH, driving a previously unrecognized pathogenic immune axis connecting dysregulated B cells to T-cell-mediated endothelial injury. BAFF inhibition may represent a therapeutic strategy for SLE-PAH.

title: “You start the day you get a job”: a life-course perspective on retirement preparedness among Ugandan academics
abstract: Purpose The study aimed to explore how academic staff in Ugandan public institutions understand the concept of retirement preparedness throughout their life course, with a focus on the influence of timing, financial knowledge, social influence and personal attitudes. Design/methodology/approach Using a life-course conceptual model, we carried out semi-structured interviews with 13 university academic staff from eight public universities in Uganda. The participants were purposively selected, and the data were analysed for themes using ATLAS.ti 25 software, paying attention to temporality, agency and relational embeddedness in which planning takes place. Findings Three main themes emerged, namely: “Early Thinking, Better Planning”, “Learning from Others” and “Living Forward”. Gender roles and the instability of the institution also influenced how people prepared for retirement. Practical implications These results suggest that retirement preparedness should also be understood through the lenses of health management, social inclusion and life course timing, in addition to the financial perspective. Policymakers should invest in comprehensive models of retirement planning that are more context-sensitive. Originality/value The study adds to life-course theory and contributes to the gerontological literature by focusing on the real-life experiences of academic staff in Uganda.

title: Yapay Zekâ Tutumunun İstihdam Edilebilirlik Algısı Üzerindeki Etkisinde Yapay Zekâ Okuryazarlığının Aracılık Rolü
abstract: Günümüzde yapay zekâ ve araçları hızlı bir şekilde gelişmektedir. Yaşamın çeşitli alanlarında olduğu gibi iş hayatı da bu durumdan etkilenmekte ve yapay zekâ, istihdam sürecini dönüştüren unsurlardan biri olarak ortaya çıkmaktadır. Çalışmanın temel amacı, bireylerin yapay zekâya yönelik tutumlarının istihdam edilebilirlik algıları üzerindeki etkisinde yapay zekâ okuryazarlığının aracı rolünü incelemektir. Çalışma, nicel araştırma yaklaşımına dayalı kesitsel bir araştırma olarak tasarlanmıştır. Bu doğrultuda, Türkiye’deki bir devlet üniversitesinde öğrenim gören 592 lisans ve ön lisans öğrencisinden kolayda örnekleme yöntemi kullanılarak anket aracılıyla veri toplanmıştır. Yapılan regresyon ve aracılık analizleri neticesinde yapay zekâya yönelik olumlu tutumun yapay zekâ okuryazarlığını artırarak istihdam edilebilirlik algısını olumlu yönde etkilediği tespit edilmiştir. Bu bulgu bireylerin istihdam edilebilirlik algısının, yapay zekâya yönelik tutumlarının yanı sıra söz konusu teknolojiyi verimli bir biçimde kullanma düzeyine de bağlı olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır. Bu çalışma ile yapay zekâ tutumu ve okuryazarlığının istihdam edilebilirlik algısı üzerindeki rolüne dikkat çekilerek istihdam edilebilirliği artırmanın bir yolu olarak yapay zekânın önemi vurgulanmaktadır. Yapay zekâ okuryazarlığının, yapay zekâya yönelik olumlu tutum ile istihdam edilebilirlik algısı arasında aracı bir rol üstlendiğinin ampirik olarak kanıtlanması, bireylerin iş piyasasındaki konumlarını anlamada sadece teknolojiye yönelik genel eğilimlerin değil, somut bilgi ve beceri düzeylerinin de belirleyici olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır.

title: When more is not better: how business model portfolios drive performance in multi-business model entrepreneurial firms
journal: Journal of Small Business and Enterprise Development
abstract: Purpose Drawing on configuration theory, this study examines how different combinations of business model (BM) design themes shape the financial performance of entrepreneurial firms that simultaneously adopt multiple business models. We thus depart from typical BM research that investigates design themes in isolation to focus on how configurations of design themes differentially influence the performance of firms that operate BM portfolios. Design/methodology/approach We employ fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to test whether specific configurations of BM design themes relate to high financial performance. fsQCA aligns well with the main objectives of this study because it captures equifinality and causal complexity, allowing for the empirical examination of multiple configurations that can lead to high performance. The final sample consists of 107 UK software firms characterized by rapid innovation adoption and frequent use of BM portfolios. Findings The results indicate three distinct configurations that relate to high financial performance: (1) novelty combined with the absence of customer lock-in and product/service complementarities; (2) novelty combined with efficiency and the absence of product/service complementarities; and (3) novelty combined with customer lock-in and product/service complementarities in the absence of efficiency. Across all these configurations, novelty clearly emerges as a core BM theme. Notably, we do not find a configuration in which all four BM design themes are present, suggesting that high performance relates with specific combinations rather than the cumulative presence of all themes. Research limitations/implications This study contributes to BM literature by providing new theoretical arguments and evidence on how firms with BM portfolios can realize performance benefits. We therefore extend pertinent BM theory to the portfolio level and shift scholarly attention from optimizing individual BMs to understanding how design themes are configured across multiple BMs within the same firm. Practical implications Our findings show how software firms can combine different design themes in their BM portfolio to achieve high performance. The results suggest that performance benefits relate to specific combinations of novelty, efficiency, customer lock-in, and product/service complementarities. Although our findings are specific to the context of UK software companies, they provide managers with a practical guide on how to design their BM portfolios when pursuing high financial performance. Originality/value Despite the growing attention to the design of business models, our understanding of BM portfolios in entrepreneurial firms remains limited. This study advances this stream of literature by theorizing and empirically examining configurations of BM design themes (novelty, efficiency, customer lock-in and product/service complementarities) at the portfolio level. Based on configuration theory, it moves beyond analyzing individual design themes in isolation and contributes to a more nuanced understanding of how combinations of BM design themes are associated with high performance.

title: Waste management efficiency in Europe: evidence from low-efficiency countries
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the dynamic efficiency of municipal waste management systems across 28 European countries during the period 2010–2022 and to identify the structural determinants of efficiency differences to support evidence-based environmental policy and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The study employs DEA Window analysis (CCR framework) to assess the dynamic efficiency of municipal waste-management systems across 28 European countries during 2010–2022. The evaluation is based on one input and four output indicators derived from the European Circular Economy Monitoring Framework. Additional BCC sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulations are conducted to assess the robustness of the efficiency rankings. In the second stage, a panel fractional logit model is used to identify the structural determinants of efficiency in a group of structurally comparable low-efficiency countries. Findings The results reveal pronounced and persistent cross-country disparities in waste management efficiency across Europe. Countries with stronger institutional and infrastructural capacity consistently operate closer to the efficiency frontier, whereas structurally constrained countries exhibit persistent inefficiencies, particularly in recycling and material recovery. Although gradual improvements are observed over time, the convergence toward best-practice benchmarks remains limited. Panel fractional logit analysis further indicates that institutional quality exerts a stronger influence on efficiency than conventional macroeconomic or innovation-related factors. Originality/value This paper contributes by developing an integrated analytical framework that combines dynamic DEA Window benchmarking, robustness assessment, and panel fractional response modeling to explain persistent structural differences in waste-management efficiency across European countries. Beyond measuring efficiency, the proposed framework supports evidence-based decision-making by identifying structural performance gaps, their institutional drivers, and differentiated policy priorities for countries at different stages of circular-economy transition.

title: The role of cadherins and catenins in endometrial function and embryo implantation: A comprehensive review
abstract: Cadherins and catenins are essential transmembrane proteins and cytoplasmic binding partners that mediate cell–cell adhesion, intracellular signaling, and the maintenance of tissue architecture. Their coordinated functions are central to endometrial biology and embryo implantation, a process that requires complex cell–cell interactions and tissue remodeling for pregnancy to be established. In this review, we summarize current evidence on the molecular mechanisms through which cadherins and catenins regulate endometrial receptivity and support embryo attachment to maternal tissue. We also discuss how advances in molecular biology and reproductive medicine have clarified the roles of cadherin–catenin complexes in cell adhesion, intracellular signaling, including Wnt/β-catenin signaling, and the regulation of trophoblast invasion. In addition, we examine the potential clinical relevance of dysfunction in these complexes, which has been associated with implantation failure and infertility. A clearer understanding of cadherin–catenin function in the endometrium may support the development of diagnostic tools and therapeutic targets for infertility.

title: Sustainable bio-based concrete: material innovations, durability challenges and life cycle perspectives
journal: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology
abstract: Purpose This review presents a critical evaluation of bio-based and bio-enabled cementitious systems as solutions for lowering resource use and climate change impact without compromising performance. This study aims to review their components based on the processing of the components, their interaction with the matrix, the mechanical properties, durability performance and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). Design/methodology/approach This research uses a structured narrative review methodology based on peer-reviewed sources from the Scopus database, which includes peer-reviewed English-language literature from the years 2005 to 2025. Data were categorized in terms of material type, manufacturing process, density and test age, mechanical and durability performance and LCA functional unit, system boundary, biogenic carbon handling, energy and water metrics. Findings What emerges is an inherent performance-functional property balance, rather than a universally superior material per se. Low-density materials made from hemp, straw, wood and cork possess excellent insulating capabilities, yet generally do not have structural properties. Surface-treated fibers, biochar and Microbial-Induced Carbonate Precipitation (MICP) improve crack prevention, transport resistance and self-healing after cracking; however, some environmental gains might be compromised due to the use of increased chemicals and additional energy requirements. Results obtained in the process of comparative LCA are very much dependent on the choice of the functional unit, system boundaries, considered lifetime, allocation and biogenic carbon assumptions. Originality/value This review integrates a taxonomy-based approach linking feedstock choice and processing approaches to performance, durability and environmental impacts. Evidence tables of three themes include processing of constituents, mechanical properties and durability data and LCA studies. Moreover, there is a cross-theme research agenda highlighting the processes involved in design, standardization and scaling up.

title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

title: “I wouldn’t forgive me”: apology, forgiveness from others, and self-forgiveness among incarcerated men and women
